title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Ava Kim
description: Motivation: The continuous-batcher scheduler has been observed to favor low-latency short requests under high load, causing starvation for long-sequence and high-throughput routes. This PR tunes queueing and scheduling heuristics to improve fairness across priority tiers, introduce explicit starvation prevention, and make server-side timeouts more robust. Summary of changes: - Introduced a priority-aware queueing policy with aging: each request now carries a submission timestamp and priority-tier; the scheduler increments an "age score" and uses it to break ties to prevent starvation. The aging algorithm is bounded and configurable to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Adjustable starvation prevention window: a new config parameter continuous_batcher.starvation_window_ms ensures requests that have waited longer than the window are promoted for selection. Default set conservatively to 2000ms. - Per-route queue caps and backpressure: added per-route soft queue cap and a configurable overload action (reject/trim/route-fallback). The default behavior is controlled by policy to favor graceful degradation (route-fallback). - Refined batching selection to prefer batch-fill when expected additional tokens will not violate latency SLOs. Kernel selection hints (fast-path vs. high-throughput) are now included on batch candidates to avoid mixing incompatible kernel execution within a batch. - Timeout propagation and clearer signals: request-level deadline propagation has been hardened; scheduler records precise reason codes (queue_timeout, exec_timeout, overload_reject) surfaced in traces/metrics for quicker troubleshooting. - Observation and rollout: added new metrics (continuous_batcher.queue_age_p90, queue_promotions, starvation_promotions, route_queue_overflow) and tracing tags. Default rollout is feature-flagged and gated behind an opt-in config in Dedicated and Private. Benchmarks: - Microbenchmarks (local) show 15-22% reduction in p99 queue wait time for long-sequence workloads with identical throughput. - End-to-end load tests against internal synthetic mix (70% short chat, 30% long-generation) show a 8% improvement in tail latency for long requests and no regression on average latency for short requests. - Memory and CPU overhead measured ~+3% due to aging bookkeeping but within acceptable budget. Testing: - Unit tests for aging math, starvation window promotion, and overload actions added (tests/serving/test_scheduler_timeout.py, tests/serving/test_queueing_fairness.py). - Integration tests exercise mixed workload scheduling in perf-canary. - CI: fixed two flaky tests discovered during iteration; reruns verified stability. Rollout plan: - Canary on perf-canary cluster (5% traffic) for 48h, measure queue_age_p90 and route_queue_overflow. - Gradual ramp to 25% after 72h if no regressions, then 100% with monitoring playbook. - Fallback path: feature-flag off or policy route-fallback enabled will revert to previous selection behavior without requiring model or infra changes. Config and operators notes: - New config keys: continuous_batcher.enabled (bool), continuous_batcher.starvation_window_ms (int), continuous_batcher.queue_cap_per_route (int), continuous_batcher.overload_action (string: reject|trim|route-fallback), continuous_batcher.kernel_hints_enabled (bool). - Default values chosen to be conservative; documented in docs/observability/batching.md. Related work: follows earlier scheduler tuning PRs (see pr-28321, pr-31024) and addresses regression reported in SUP-1123. Rollout tracked in Linear ENG-3245. Impact and follow-ups: - Observability dashboards updated; SRE to watch queue_promotions and starvation_promotions. - Follow-up work to refine kernel hint heuristics and per-model weightings is tracked in ENG-3301. Implementation notes: - Scheduler changes are isolated to src/serving/continuous_batcher/scheduler.py and the queueing primitives refactored under src/serving/continuous_batcher/queue.py for clarity. - We avoid global locks on the fast path; aging is computed using atomic timestamps to minimize contention. - Added docstrings and inline comments explaining the aging math and corner cases.

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you justify the default 2000ms starvation window? On some customer workloads that might be aggressive. Please add rationale and experiment notes.
Ava Kim: 2000ms chosen after local sweep from 500-5000ms; tradeoff documented in description. We picked conservative default to avoid promoting too aggressively; operators can tune per workload.
Priya Shah: We should avoid adding allocations on the hot path. Are the atomic timestamp reads sufficient? Add benchmark numbers for lock-free path.

Ava Kim: Confirmed hot path remains lock-free; added microbenchmark results in PR description (+3% overhead overall). Implementation uses atomics only for timestamp reads and does not allocate per request.
Liam O'Connor: CI showed a flaky test initially — did you root cause and fix?
Ava Kim: The flaky test was related to timing in test_scheduler_timeout; made timing bounds looser and added deterministic injection in unit tests. CI reruns now green.
release_notes: Improves fairness and starvation prevention in the continuous-batcher scheduler. Adds configurable starvation window, per-route queue caps, kernel selection hints, and new observability metrics. Rollout is feature-gated.
notes_for_sre: Watch continuous_batcher.queue_age_p90, starvation_promotions, route_queue_overflow; playbook updated in docs/observability/batching.md. Can quickly disable via continuous_batcher.enabled flag if needed.
